newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Asian Metals - Seoul aluminium premiums seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Asian Metals - Seoul aluminium premiums seen rising.

text.p: South Korean aluminium premiums are expected to rise to $95-$100 per tonne over London Metal Exchange (LME) cash prices for July-September shipment in line with bullish Japanese import premiums, traders in Seoul said.
This compared with $88 a tonne over LME cash prices basis CIF Pusan for the second quarter shipment, they said.

In Japan, aluminium importers are negotiating this week with foreign aluminium producers for July-September term contracts, which some traders say are likely to be set around $85 to $90 per tonne but possibly as high as $95 a tonne over LME cash prices.
The Japanese premiums are expected to be decided early next week.
"Aluminium premiums for third quarter shipment are likely to go up around $10 a tonne from the previous quarter due to strong Japanese premiums," a trader with Samsung Corp said.
The trader said the premiums for Japanese buyers have been a benchmark for the deals of South Korean importers.

South Korean aluminium importers began negotiating for aluminium import premiums with foreign suppliers from the end of last week and are expected to last until early next month, a trader with Daewoo Corp said.
Traders said the metal's premiums in spot trade have been as high as $105 a tonne over LME cash prices.
"Some foreign suppliers have asked for premiums of up to $105 a tonne for spot trade," a trader with a major trading firm said.
He said his company was recently asked for a premium of $98 a tonne over LME cash prices by a Singapore trader.

Traders said the rise of aluminium import premiums reflected strong global demand for the metal, coupled with low LME stocks and firm U.S. Midwest premiums. They said the domestic metal business was still slumping due to a series of domestic economic woes.
Domestic aluminium prices were unchanged at 1.53 million won a tonne over the past week and copper prices were flat at 2,354,000 won .
Zinc and lead prices were also unchanged at 1,283,000 won a tonne and at 708,000 won respectively.
